title: 《HKEx》- 01952 雲頂新耀 - 有關戰略合作框架協議之持續關連交易
text:
[PDF PAGE 1]
香港交易及結算所有限公司及香港聯合交易所有限公司對本公告的內容概不負責，對其準確性或
完整性亦不發表任何聲明，並明確表示，概不對因本公告全部或任何部份內容而產生或因倚賴該
等內容而引致的任何損失承擔任何責任。
（於開曼群島註冊成立的有限公司）
（股份代號：1952）
Everest Medicines Limited
雲 頂 新 耀 有 限 公 司
有關戰略合作框架協議之
持續關連交易
董事會欣然宣佈，於2026年9月9日，該附屬公司（ 為本公司全資附屬公司 ）與海森
訂立戰略合作框架協議，據此，訂約雙方同意就產品在中國的供應、分銷及相關
製造與商業化建立框架。本集團一直在中國發展其藥品分銷及供應鏈能力，並預
計將於2026年底在中國獲得藥品經營許可。在取得相關許可後，本集團擬按照適
用的GSP要求開展藥品經營及分銷活動。就此而言，本集團擬透過與海森（ 作為其
合作夥伴 ）訂立的戰略合作框架協議，利用其GSP平台、商業基礎設施及生產相關
資源，以及海森集團持有或獲授權的各類產品，共同拓展產品在該地區的商業服
務、分銷及生產相關合作。戰略合作框架協議的主要條款載列如下。
戰略合作框架協議
日期： 2026年9月9日
訂約方： (i) 該附屬公司；及
(ii) 海森
期限
在訂約雙方遵守適用法律（ 包括但不限於上市規則 ）的前提下，戰略合作框架協議
的期限自生效日期起開始，並將持續有效至2028年12月31日止，除非根據其條款
提前終止。在遵守適用上市規則的前提下，戰略合作框架協議將自動重續三年，
– 1 –

[PDF PAGE 2]
除非(i)任何一方向另一方發出至少六個月的事先不重續書面通知，或(ii)適用法律
禁止有關自動重續。於戰略合作框架協議的期限屆滿前，董事會將重新評估戰略
合作框架協議的條款及條件，而本公司將重新遵守上市規則項下規管關連交易的
相關規則。
標的事項
根據戰略合作框架協議，訂約雙方同意就產品在中國的分銷、生產及商業化進行
合作，包括透過以下合作模式：(i)商業化服務模式；(ii)總分銷模式；(iii)產銷模
式 ； 及 (iv) 潛 在 合 作 模 式 。 各 合 作 模 式 的 主 要 條 款 載 列 如 下 。 訂 約 雙 方 將 考 慮 各
產品的上市許可持有人、生產安排、供應狀況、業務計劃、渠道政策、合作區域
及適用監管要求，以釐定於相關期間採用的適當合作模式。有關交易的性質及定
價將取決於具體合作安排，並將由訂約雙方在考慮上述因素後經公平磋商釐定。
商業化服務模式
根據商業化服務模式，本集團將繼續根據現有商業化服務協議，於中國就指定產
品提供商業化服務。有關商業化服務包括（ 其中包括 ）本地分銷及推廣服務、全國
營銷及推廣服務、分銷商甄選及管理服務、銷售預測服務、醫院招標服務及其他
商業活動。有關現有商業化服務協議的進一步詳情，請參閱本公司日期為2025年
12月11日的公告及本公司日期為2026年2月4日的通函。為免生疑問，現有商業化
服務協議的條款維持不變且繼續有效。
總分銷模式
訂約雙方可制定總分銷模式，據此，海森集團將委任本集團相關成員公司為指定
產品在指定地區全部或部分區域內的總分銷商。本集團將向海森或其指定供應商
採購產品，並將以自身名義進行進口（ 倘適用 ）、分銷、銷售、渠道管理以及就有
關產品進行其他商業化活動，而無須承擔須由適用上市許可持有人承擔的任何法
定責任。
總 分銷 模式 可採 取 以下 形式 ：(i) 全 面一 般分 銷 安排 ，據 此， 本集 團 負責 進口（ 倘
適用 ）、管理渠道及銷售產品；或(ii)渠道分銷安排，據此，本集團主要負責產品
採購、倉儲、交付及分銷，而推廣、市場准入及其他商業化服務則由相關服務供
– 2 –

[PDF PAGE 3]
應 商 根 據 商 業 化 服 務 模 式 進 行 。 具 體 安 排 應 以 訂 約 雙 方 訂 立 的 相 關 項 目 協 議
為準。
產銷模式
訂約雙方可制定產銷模式，據此，本集團將向海森集團或其指定供應商採購生產
物 料 ， 並 就 產 品 進 行 國 內 二 次 包 裝 、 合 約 製 造 、 生 產 準 備 、 技 術 轉 移 、 製 程 驗
證、監管申報支援及相關活動。本集團隨後將以自身名義在協定地區就有關產品
進行分銷、銷售及商業化，而無須承擔須由適用上市許可持有人承擔的任何法定
責任。
潛在合作模式
根據潛在合作模式，海森集團的相關實體（ 作為產品商業權所有人 ）將授權本集團
擔任協定地區指定產品的總分銷商及商業化服務提供商。本集團將直接向適用上
市許可持有人採購產品，並以自身名義進行分銷、銷售、渠道管理、產品推廣及
其他協定的商業化服務，而無須承擔須由適用上市許可持有人承擔的任何法定責
任。具體條款應以訂約雙方訂立的項目分協議或三方商業合作協議為準。
定價政策
戰略合作框架協議項下擬進行交易的定價及結算安排將按公平交易原則及按一般
商業條款釐定。產品的採購價格將主要參照（ 如有 ）現行市場基準釐定，包括公開
招標價格、線上掛網價格、醫療保險報銷標準及市場銷售價格。倘並無直接可比
價格，訂約雙方將考慮其他客觀市場基準，包括本集團承擔的職能及風險以及同
類活動的市場分銷利潤率。
在產銷模式下，物料或產品的採購價格以及技術轉移、驗證、監管申報支援或生
產準備的任何一次性費用，將參照（ 倘適用 ）過往獨立交易價格、獨立第三方就類
似產品或服務所收取的價格、相關成本及市場利潤率，並按公平交易原則釐定。
訂約雙方將訂立具體協議，其中載明適用的價格、費用及付款條款。

總分銷模式、產銷模式或潛在合作模式下並無任何過往交易。

年度上限的基準
建議年度上限主要參考以下因素釐定：(i)相關安排的預期開始時間，而2026年反
映初始的部分年度期間；(ii)本集團每年對產品的估計採購量；(iii)根據歷史價格
及 現 有 市 場 基 準 計 算 的 預 期 單 位 採 購 價 格 ； (iv) 與 生 產 準 備 、 技 術 轉 移 、 驗 證 或
相關活動有關的估計一次性成本或費用（ 倘適用 ）；及(v)因應產品需求、採購量及
市場價格的正常波動而預留的合理緩衝空間。概括而言，年度上限乃按相關產品
的預期採購量乘以預期單位採購價格，再加計任何適用的一次性費用及上述緩衝
額而計算得出。2027年的年度上限較2026年有所增加，反映預期將由2026年初始
的部分年度實施過渡至全年營運，以及預期所涵蓋產品的數量及╱或銷量將有所
擴大。2028年的進一步增加則反映預計相關業務量將逐步提升。

持續關連交易的內部控制
本公司已就持續關連交易採納並實施一系列內部控制措施，而董事會及本公司各
內部部門負責對持續關連交易進行控制及管理。內部控制措施的詳情如下：
(i) 董事會及本公司各內部部門（ 包括財務、法務及合規以及業務營運部 ）將共同
負責每年評估戰略合作框架協議的條款，尤其是該協議的定價政策及年度上
限的公平性及合理性；
(ii) 業務營運部及財務部已經並將會繼續每季度密切監控戰略合作框架協議項下
持續關連交易的實際交易金額。倘累計實際交易金額及已訂立訂單預計將達
到 相 關 年 度 上 限 的 80 % ， 或 業 務 營 運 部 及 財 務 部 預 期 相 關 業 務 營 運 將 會 擴
大，並可能在短期內耗盡年度上限的相當部分，則應立即將有關事項呈報本
公司法務、財務、公司秘書及業務部進行評估。本公司隨後將評估是否有需
要修訂現有年度上限，如有需要，則將根據本公司相關內部程序修訂年度上
限，並重新遵守上市規則的規定；
(iii) 在本公司訂立戰略合作框架協議項下的任何交易前，負責業務單位須確保遵

戰略合作框架協議須遵守上市規則第14A章項下申報、公告、年度審閱及獨立股

自願公告
最新業務情況
有關星必妥®用於治療成人陣發性室上性心動過速急性症狀發作
轉復為竇性心律的新藥上市申請在中國獲批
本公告由雲頂新耀有限公司（「本公司」）自願作出，以向本公司股東及潛在投資者
提供有關最新業務資料。
本 公 司 董 事 會（「董 事 會」）欣 然 宣 佈 ， 中 國 國 家 藥 品 監 督 管 理 局 (NMPA) 已 批 准 星
必妥®（ 艾曲帕米鼻噴霧劑 ）的新藥上市許可申請，用於治療成人陣發性室上性心
動過速（「PSVT」）急性症狀發作，轉復為竇性心律。
此次獲批是基於星必妥®全球關鍵III期RAPID臨床研究和中國III期JX 02002臨床研
究所取得的數據結果。兩項研究均達到了方案預設的主要終點。其中，在關鍵性
III期RAPID臨床研究中，判定為PSVT發作的參與者（ N = 99 ）自行使用星必妥®後有
64 %在給藥30分鐘內從室上性心動過速轉為竇性心律，而安慰劑組（ N = 85 ）為31 %
（ HR = 2.62；95 % CI：1.66 – 4.15；p50.001 ），相關研究結果已於2023年發表於
《 柳 葉 刀 》雜 誌 。 在 中 國 I I I 期 JX 02002 臨 床 研 究 中 ， 判 定 為 PSVT 發 作 的 參 與 者
（ N = 84 ）自行使用星必妥®，與安慰劑給藥組（ N = 84 ）相比，PSVT轉復為竇性心律
方 面 具 有 顯 著 優 效 性（ HR = 3.002 ； p = 0.0005 ）。 在 所 有 I I I 期 臨 床 研 究 中 ， 星 必
妥®總體耐受性良好，給藥後24小時內均未觀察到嚴重不良事件（ SAEs ）。此前，
星必妥®已於2025年12月獲得美國食品藥品監督管理局（ FDA ）批准，成為30多年
來首款且唯一獲批用於成人PSVT急性症狀發作治療的創新療法。
– 1 –

[PDF PAGE 2]
作為 本公 司在 心血 管疾 病領 域首個 獲批 的創 新藥 物， 星必 妥®進一 步豐 富了 本公
司的創新產品組合。此次獲批是本公司創新產品商業化戰略持續兌現的又一重要
里程碑，充分彰顯了本公司持續整合全球創新資源、加速創新成果轉化和高效推
動商業化落地的能力。
有關PSVT之資料
PSVT是一類以突發突止為主要特徵的快速性心律失常，發作期間心率顯著增快且
節律規則，持續時間可從數分鐘至數小時不等。患者常出現心悸、胸悶、頭暈、
乏力等症狀，部分患者伴有明顯焦慮、恐懼感，嚴重影響生活品質。PSVT急性發
作的治療缺乏安全、便捷、可在院外自行使用的快速終止藥物，患者在發作時往
往只能等待症狀自行緩解或尋求醫療救治，缺乏真正意義上的「應急自救」治療。
在中國，每1000人中約有2.3至4人患有PSVT，估計總患者人數為300至600萬，存
在顯著未滿足的臨床需求。
有關星必妥®（艾曲帕米鼻噴霧劑）之資料
星必妥®是一款由Milestone Pharmaceuticals, Inc.（ Nasdaq：MIST ）研發的新型、速效
的鈣離子通道阻滯劑，採用可攜式鼻噴霧劑給藥，具備快速起效、便捷給藥的特
點 ， 是 目 前 唯 一 可 由 PSVT 患 者 在 症 狀 發 作 時 自 行 給 藥 並 實 現 快 速 終 止 發 作 的 藥
物。星必妥®最早可於給藥後5分鐘開始起效，近三分之二的患者可在30分鐘內恢
復竇性心律，顯著減少了對額外急救醫療干預的需求，填補了中國PSVT患者急性
發作時院外「應急自救」的空白。

截至2026年6月30日止六個月及最後可行日期，雲頂新耀持續通過推進商業化產品組合、拓展研發管線以及加速亞太區域佈局，
踐行其2030戰略。報告期內，公司繼續鞏固商業化平台，推動多項臨床階段及商業化資產的進展，並通過一系列戰略性的業務
拓展交易與合作豐富產品組合。
報告期內的主要成就包括：耐賦康®商業化及真實世界研究進展勢頭強勁；維適平®獲得中國大陸新藥上市許可申請並商業化上市；
通過多項授權許可、收購及合作協議擴充產品管線；通過收購海森生物製藥（新加坡）有限公司夯實了亞太區域商業化平台；成
功完成了首款擁有全球權益產品的對外授權交易。同時，多個後期臨床開發項目取得進展以及公司個性化mRNA腫瘤疫苗
EVM16發佈積極的首批人體臨床試驗數據。這些進展進一步夯實了雲頂新耀多元化的產品組合，並增強了其在亞太市場的商業
化及開發佈局，引領公司向成為該地區領先生物製藥公司的長期戰略目標邁進。
腎科管線產品組合
雲頂新耀已建立起行業領先的腎病領域產品組合，全面覆蓋商業化產品、後期開發項目及創新診斷技術。耐賦康®(NEFECON®)
是中國目前首個且唯一獲得完全批准的IgA 腎病(IgAN)治療藥物，已成為IgAN基石產品，在此基礎上，公司的腎病管線已拓展
至包括針對自身免疫性腎小球疾病及透析相關併發症的差異化資產。通過戰略性業務拓展的驅動，公司正在構建一個全面的腎
病診療平台，旨在滿足多種腎科領域適應症尚未被滿足的醫療需求，並鞏固其在中國及亞太地區腎病治療領域的領導地位。
耐賦康®(NEFECON®)是布地奈德腸溶膠囊，作為全球首個對因治療IgA腎病的藥物，是靶向腸道黏膜B細胞的免疫調節劑，能
減少50%腎功能下降，在中國人群中能延緩腎功能衰退達66%，預計將疾病進展至透析或腎移植的時間延緩12.8年。同時布地
奈德首過代謝程度達90%，具有良好的安全性。耐賦康®專為IgA腎病患者研製，每顆膠囊含布地奈德4mg，通過特殊的遲釋及
緩釋雙重制劑工藝，將布地奈德靶向釋放於迴腸末端的黏膜B細胞（包括派爾集合淋巴結），膠囊溶解後，三層包衣微丸持續穩
定釋放布地奈德，高濃度覆蓋整個靶區域，從而減少誘發IgA腎病的半乳糖缺陷的IgA1抗體(Gd-IgA1)產生，進而干預發病機制
上游階段，達到治療IgA腎病的作用。耐賦康®於2023年11月獲得中國國家藥品監督管理局(NMPA)批准用於治療原發性IgA腎病，
並於2024年5月在中國大陸上市。自2025年1月起，耐賦康®(NEFECON®)已正式納入國家醫保藥品目錄「( NRDL」)，大幅提升
了這一疾病首創藥物的患者可及性。
— 2026年3月，在2026年國際腎臟病學會(ISN)世界腎臟病大會(WCN 2026)上，耐賦康®展示10項來自中國的最新研究成果，
進一步展現其在IgA腎病治療領域的深入研究進展。此次公佈的研究數據來自中國多家頂尖醫院的臨床實踐，從多個維度
深入探討了耐賦康®在IgA腎病對因治療和儘早治療中的療效和安全性，進一步充實了「對因治療、儘早治療、長期治療」
的治療策略。

業務摘要
— 2026年5月，首部《IgA腎病臨床實踐60問（2026版）》專家共識發佈，此次重磅發佈為我國IgA腎病臨床診療提供了系統性、
規範化的臨床實踐指引。耐賦康®作為全球首個IgA腎病對因治療藥物，憑藉獨特的腸道靶向機制，從源頭干預IgA腎病的
發生與進展，並依託充分的循證醫學證據，成為該共識推薦的核心治療藥物，推動IgA腎病源頭靶向治療的規範化臨床實踐。
— 2026年6月，第63屆歐洲腎臟協會大會(ERA 2026)上，耐賦康®展示了23項來自全球及中國的最新真實世界研究成果，
涵蓋多個關鍵維度，持續驗證了其在對因治療、儘早治療、長期治療等方面的療效與安全性，進一步夯實其臨床價值，為
全球IgA腎病患者長期規範化管理提供堅實的循證依據，鞏固其在IgA腎病對因一線治療的基石地位。
— 2026年6月，公司與海南合瑞製藥股份有限公司（「海南合瑞」）就耐賦康®相關專利達成諒解，並就海南合瑞於2025年12
月獲得中國國家藥品監督管理局批准的布地奈德腸溶膠囊開展商業化合作。

斷並追蹤病程進展的檢測方法。
EVER001（希布替尼）是新一代創新性的共價可逆BTK抑制劑，潛在用於治療包括原發性膜性腎病、IgA腎病、微小病變性腎病、
局灶節段性腎小球硬化和狼瘡性腎炎等腎臟疾病在內的自身免疫性腎病。與共價不可逆BTK抑制劑相比，EVER001作為一款潛
在的同類最佳產品，在保持高活性的同時具有高選擇性，避免持續抑制帶來的毒副作用。
— 2026年6月，公司宣佈與Travere Therapeutics, Inc.（「Travere Therapeutics」）達成獨家授權許可與合作協議。根據協議，
Travere Therapeutics將獲得EVER001除大中華區及部分東南亞國家以外區域的獨家開發及商業化權益。此次合作將加速
EVER001的全球臨床開發與商業化進程，為全球腎病患者帶來創新治療選擇。
— 2026年6月，公司宣佈在第63屆歐洲腎臟協會大會(ERA 2026)上，以口頭報告的形式公佈了EVER001用於治療原發性膜

報告期後成就及預期里程碑：
— 2026年7月，公司宣佈，已根據協議條款完成與Travere Therapeutics關於EVER001的獨家授權許可與合作協議交割，表

將共同推進EVER001的後續開發與商業化。
MT1013是一款全球首創的雙靶點受體激動劑多肽，可同時靶向鈣敏感受體(CaSR)及成骨生長肽(OGP)受體，開發主要用於治療

在臨床階段的腎科管線中，希布替尼(EVER001)治療原發性膜性腎病的52周Ib/IIa期數據亮相第63屆歐洲腎臟協會大會(ERA 
2026)，進一步驗證了其在自身免疫性腎臟疾病領域的廣闊潛力。基於上述積極數據，公司已在國內啟動一項籃式臨床試驗，評
估希布替尼在局灶節段性腎小球硬化(FSGS)、微小病變型腎病(MCD)及IgA腎病(IgAN)中的療效和安全性。2026年下半年，隨著
海外授權交易的交割完成，我們將與合作夥伴Travere Therapeutics共同制定希布替尼下一步的全球開發計劃。
此外，我們通過業務拓展引入的多款後期臨床資產亦穩步推進。報告期內，樂瑞泊®
（萊達西貝普）的中國Ⅲ期臨床試驗結果於
美國心臟病學會年會(ACC 2026)上公佈，充分驗證了萊達西貝普在中國已確診、或極高危或高危動脈粥樣硬化性心血管疾病
(ASCVD)的患者中持續降低低密度脂蛋白膽固醇(LDL-C)水平，並顯示出良好的安全性；其中國新藥上市申請於2026年6月正式
獲國家藥品監督管理局受理。在眼科領域，我們的合作夥伴新橋生物於2026年3月宣佈，治療濕性年齡相關性黃斑變性的IIa期
研究取得積極頂線數據。數據顯示，VIS-101展示出起效迅速、強效持久的治療反應，及良好的安全性及耐受性，並驗證了其作
為潛在「同類最佳」持久性的臨床價值，支持其加速推進下一階段研發計劃，預計於今年下半年啟動IIb期研究。此外，星必妥（艾®

患者症狀明顯且恐懼感強。PSVT急性發作的治療缺乏安全、便捷、可在院外自行使用的快速終止藥物，使患者在發作期長期處
於「被動等待」狀態，缺乏真正意義上的「按需自救」工具。

成CAR-T三大前沿領域。

2. 會計政策變動（續）
經修訂的《國際財務報告會計準則》的性質及影響如下所述：
(a) 《國際財務報告準則》第9號及《國際財務報告準則》第7號（修訂本）「金融工具分類及計量的修訂」闡明，當實體對合
約現金流量的權利屆滿或已轉移時，金融資產即予終止確認，而金融負債則於結算日終止確認。該修訂本引入會計
政策選擇權，倘符合指定條件，則於結算日期前終止確認透過電子支付系統結算的金融負債。該修訂本闡明如何評
估具有環境、社會及管治及其他類似或有特徵的金融資產的合約現金流量特徵。此外，該修訂本闡明對具有無追索
特徵的金融資產及合約掛鈎工具分類的規定。該修訂本亦包括投資指定為按公允值計入其他全面收益的權益工具及
具有或然特徵的金融工具的額外披露。由於本集團過往年度終止確認金融資產及負債的會計政策與該修訂本一致，
且本集團並無該修訂本所述及的金融資產，因此該修訂本並未對中期簡明綜合財務資料產生任何影響。本集團將於
本集團截至2026年12月31日止年度的綜合財務報表中，就其指定為按公允值計入其他全面收益的權益投資提供額
外披露。
(b) 《國際財務報告準則》第9號及《國際財務報告準則》第7號（修訂本）「涉及依賴自然能源的電力的合約」闡明範圍內合
約「自用」規定的應用，並修訂範圍內合約現金流量對沖關係中被對沖項目的指定規定。修訂本亦包括額外披露，使
財務報表使用者能夠了解該等合約對實體財務表現及未來現金流量的影響。由於本集團並無屬於該修訂本範圍內的
任何合約，因此該修訂本並未對中期簡明綜合財務資料產生任何影響。
(c) 《國際財務報告會計準則》的年度改進 — 第11卷載列了對《國際財務報告準則》第1號、《國際財務報告準則》第7號（及
隨附的《國際財務報告準則》第7號實施指引）、《國際財務報告準則》第9號、《國際財務報告準則》第10號及《國際會
計準則》第7號的狹義修訂。該等修訂包括闡明、簡化、更正或變動，以提升相應《國際財務報告會計準則》的一致性。

截至2026年6月30日止六個月及最後可行日期，雲頂新耀持續通過推進商業化產品組合、拓展研發管線以及加速亞太區域佈局，
踐行其2030戰略。報告期內，公司繼續鞏固商業化平台，推動多項臨床階段及商業化資產的進展，並通過一系列戰略性的業務
拓展交易與合作豐富產品組合。
報告期內的主要成就包括：耐賦康®商業化及真實世界研究進展勢頭強勁；維適平®獲得中國大陸新藥上市許可申請並商業化上市；
通過多項授權許可、收購及合作協議擴充產品管線；通過收購海森生物製藥（新加坡）有限公司夯實了亞太區域商業化平台；成
功完成了首款擁有全球權益產品的對外授權交易。同時，多個後期臨床開發項目取得進展以及公司個性化mRNA腫瘤疫苗
EVM16發佈積極的首批人體臨床試驗數據。這些進展進一步夯實了雲頂新耀多元化的產品組合，並增強了其在亞太市場的商業
化及開發佈局，引領公司向成為該地區領先生物製藥公司的長期戰略目標邁進。
腎科管線產品組合
雲頂新耀已建立起行業領先的腎病領域產品組合，全面覆蓋商業化產品、後期開發項目及創新診斷技術。耐賦康®(NEFECON®)
是中國目前首個且唯一獲得完全批准的IgA 腎病(IgAN)治療藥物，已成為IgAN基石產品，在此基礎上，公司的腎病管線已拓展
至包括針對自身免疫性腎小球疾病及透析相關併發症的差異化資產。通過戰略性業務拓展的驅動，公司正在構建一個全面的腎
病診療平台，旨在滿足多種腎科領域適應症尚未被滿足的醫療需求，並鞏固其在中國及亞太地區腎病治療領域的領導地位。
耐賦康®(NEFECON®)是布地奈德腸溶膠囊，作為全球首個對因治療IgA腎病的藥物，是靶向腸道黏膜B細胞的免疫調節劑，能
減少50%腎功能下降，在中國人群中能延緩腎功能衰退達66%，預計將疾病進展至透析或腎移植的時間延緩12.8年。同時布地
奈德首過代謝程度達90%，具有良好的安全性。耐賦康®專為IgA腎病患者研製，每顆膠囊含布地奈德4mg，通過特殊的遲釋及
緩釋雙重制劑工藝，將布地奈德靶向釋放於迴腸末端的黏膜B細胞（包括派爾集合淋巴結），膠囊溶解後，三層包衣微丸持續穩
定釋放布地奈德，高濃度覆蓋整個靶區域，從而減少誘發IgA腎病的半乳糖缺陷的IgA1抗體(Gd-IgA1)產生，進而干預發病機制
上游階段，達到治療IgA腎病的作用。耐賦康®於2023年11月獲得中國國家藥品監督管理局(NMPA)批准用於治療原發性IgA腎病，
並於2024年5月在中國大陸上市。自2025年1月起，耐賦康®(NEFECON®)已正式納入國家醫保藥品目錄「( NRDL」)，大幅提升
了這一疾病首創藥物的患者可及性。
— 2026年3月，在2026年國際腎臟病學會(ISN)世界腎臟病大會(WCN 2026)上，耐賦康®展示10項來自中國的最新研究成果，
進一步展現其在IgA腎病治療領域的深入研究進展。此次公佈的研究數據來自中國多家頂尖醫院的臨床實踐，從多個維度
深入探討了耐賦康®在IgA腎病對因治療和儘早治療中的療效和安全性，進一步充實了「對因治療、儘早治療、長期治療」
的治療策略。

[PDF PAGE 6]
5
業務摘要
— 2026年5月，首部《IgA腎病臨床實踐60問（2026版）》專家共識發佈，此次重磅發佈為我國IgA腎病臨床診療提供了系統性、

在抗感染領域，產品組合包括依嘉®、羅氏芬®
（頭孢曲松）及頭孢吡肟 — 坦尼硼巴坦，可覆蓋從輕度、中度到重度的多種細菌
感染，以及多重耐藥菌導致的感染。依嘉®是公司抗感染領域的核心產品，常用於ICU、移植科、血液科等多重耐藥菌感染的重
症患者治療，與常用於社區獲得性感染治療藥物羅氏芬®形成互補。而羅氏芬®作為被臨床廣泛認可的第三代頭孢菌素，已被納
入中國國家基本藥物目錄。急重症產品組合還包括思他寧®
（生長抑素，用於急性胃腸道出血管理）和亞寧定®
（用於快速血壓控
制），均為急重症患者提供有效治療。
依嘉®
（依拉環素）是全球首個氟環素類抗菌藥物，用於治療臨床常見致病菌包括革蘭陰性菌、革蘭陽性菌、厭氧菌等以及多重耐

患者症狀明顯且恐懼感強。PSVT急性發作的治療缺乏安全、便捷、可在院外自行使用的快速終止藥物，使患者在發作期長期處
於「被動等待」狀態，缺乏真正意義上的「按需自救」工具。

2. 會計政策變動（續）
經修訂的《國際財務報告會計準則》的性質及影響如下所述：
(a) 《國際財務報告準則》第9號及《國際財務報告準則》第7號（修訂本）「金融工具分類及計量的修訂」闡明，當實體對合
約現金流量的權利屆滿或已轉移時，金融資產即予終止確認，而金融負債則於結算日終止確認。該修訂本引入會計
政策選擇權，倘符合指定條件，則於結算日期前終止確認透過電子支付系統結算的金融負債。該修訂本闡明如何評
估具有環境、社會及管治及其他類似或有特徵的金融資產的合約現金流量特徵。此外，該修訂本闡明對具有無追索
特徵的金融資產及合約掛鈎工具分類的規定。該修訂本亦包括投資指定為按公允值計入其他全面收益的權益工具及
具有或然特徵的金融工具的額外披露。由於本集團過往年度終止確認金融資產及負債的會計政策與該修訂本一致，
且本集團並無該修訂本所述及的金融資產，因此該修訂本並未對中期簡明綜合財務資料產生任何影響。本集團將於

外披露。
(b) 《國際財務報告準則》第9號及《國際財務報告準則》第7號（修訂本）「涉及依賴自然能源的電力的合約」闡明範圍內合
約「自用」規定的應用，並修訂範圍內合約現金流量對沖關係中被對沖項目的指定規定。修訂本亦包括額外披露，使
財務報表使用者能夠了解該等合約對實體財務表現及未來現金流量的影響。由於本集團並無屬於該修訂本範圍內的

The forthcoming EGM of the Company will be held by way of virtual meeting through
broadcasting at the website https://meetings.computershare.com/everestmed_2026EGM2 (the
‘‘Online Platform’’). Shareholders attending and participating in the EGM using the Online
Platform will be deemed present at, and will be counted towards the quorum of, the EGM and
they will be able to cast their votes and submit questions through the Online Platform. Unless
otherwise defined herein, terms used in this Guidance for the EGM shall have the same
meanings in the ‘‘Definitions’’ section on pages 5 to 9.
ATTENDANCE
Both registered and non-registered Shareholders will be able to attend and view a live
webcast of the EGM, raise questions and cast votes through the Online Platform.
Online Platform
The Online Platform will be opened for registered and non-registered Shareholders to log
into approximately 30 minutes prior to the commencement of the EGM and can be accessed
from any location with internet connection by a smart phone, tablet device or computer.
Shareholders should allow ample time to check into the Online Platform to complete the
related procedures.
A step-by-step ‘‘Online Meeting User Guide’’ for the login process of the EGM has been
made available on the Company’s website at www.everestmedicines.com for assistance.
Login details for registered Shareholders
For registered Shareholders, the login details for joining the EGM through the Online
Platform are provided in the notification letter that has been sent together with this circular.
Login details for non-registered Shareholders
Non-registered Shareholders who wish to attend and vote at the EGM through the Online
Platform should:
(1) contact and instruct your banks, brokers, custodians, nominees or HKSCC Nominees
Limited by which your Shares are held (collectively, the ‘‘Intermediary’’) to appoint
you as the proxies or corporate representatives to attend and vote at the EGM; and
(2) provide your email address(es) to your Intermediary before the deadline imposed by
your Intermediary.
Login details to access the Online Platform will be sent to the non-registered Shareholders
by the Company’s share registrar, Computershare Hong Kong Investor Services Limited
(‘‘Computershare’’), to the email address(es) you provided to the Intermediary. Any
nonregistered Shareholder who has provided an email address through the relevant
Intermediary for this purpose but has not received the login details by email by 9:30 a.m. on
Tuesday, 16 June 2026 should reach out to Computershare for assistance.
GUIDANCE FOR THE EGM
– 1 –

[PDF PAGE 4]
Without the login details, non-registered Shareholders will not be able to attend,
participate or vote at the EGM. Non-registered Shareholders should therefore give clear and
specific instructions to their Intermediary in respect of both (1) and (2) above.
Login details for duly appointed proxies or corporate representatives
Login details to access the Online Platform will be sent by Computershare to the email
address(es) of the proxies provided in the returned forms of proxy.
For corporate Shareholders who wish to appoint representatives to attend, participate and
vote at the EGM on their behalf through the Online Platform, please call the service hotline of
Computershare at (852) 2862 8555 during business hours from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. (Hong
Kong time) from Monday to Friday, excluding Hong Kong public holidays for arrangements.
Any proxy or corporate representative who has not received the login details by email by
9:30 a.m. on Tuesday, 16 June 2026 should reach out to Computershare for assistance.
Login details for new registered Shareholders
For new registered Shareholders (who registered after the dispatch date of the EGM
documents but are still entitled to attend, participate and vote at the EGM), login details can be
obtained by request from Computershare with the contact details below:
Computershare Hong Kong Investor Services Limited
17M Floor, Hopewell Centre, 183 Queen’s Road East, Wanchai, Hong Kong
Tel: (852) 2862 8555
Fax: (852) 2865 0990
Website: www.computershare.com/hk/contact
POINTS TO NOTE
Registered and non-registered Shareholders should note that only one device is allowed in
respect of each set of login details. Please also keep the login details in safe custody for use at
the EGM and do not disclose them to anyone else. Neither the Company nor its agents assume
any obligation or liability whatsoever in connection with the transmission of the login details
or any use of the login details for voting or otherwise. Shareholders should also note that an
active and stable internet connection is required in order to allow them to participate, vote and
submit questions at the EGM through the Online Platform. It is the users’ own responsibility to
ensure that they have a sufficient and stable internet connection.
PROXY APPOINTMENT AND VOTING
Voting by Proxy
A Shareholder who is entitled to attend and vote at the EGM is entitled to appoint a proxy
to exercise the Shareholder’s rights at the EGM. A proxy who needs not be a Shareholder of
the Company may attend, speak and vote instead of the Shareholder.

Basis of the consideration
The consideration for the Acquisition comprises (i) the acquisition of the Sale Share
by the Purchaser; and (ii) the taking of assignment of the Shareholder Loan by the
Purchaser pursuant to the Share Purchase Agreement and was agreed between the parties
after arm’s length negotiations taking into account various factors, including:
(i) the valuation of the equity value of the Target Company before the Shareholder
Loan as of 31 March 2026 of approximately US$323,000,000 (approximately
RMB2,270,302,000) (the ‘‘Appraised Value’’) as assessed by an independent
valuer using the market approach, details of which are set out below;
(ii) the historical financial information of the Target Company; and
(iii) the reasons for and benefits of the Acquisition as set out in the paragraph
headed ‘‘Reasons for and Benefits of the Share Purchase Agreement’’.
In assessing the consideration, the parties considered the Acquisition as a whole
commercial arrangement, which comprises (i) the acquisition of the entire equity interest
in the Target Company; and (ii) the Purchaser’s assumption of the Shareholder Loan by
assignment. As such, the parties considered the consideration of the Acquisition on a
combined basis, taking into account both the equity interest of the Target Company and
the assumption of the Shareholder Loan by the Purchaser.
The Appraised Value, being a valuation of the equity value of the Target Company
before the Shareholder Loan (i.e. not deducting the Shareholder Loan in calculating the
equity value of the Shareholder Loan) provided a reasonable reference point as it more
accurately reflects the underlying business performance of the Target Company without
being affected by how the Target Company was financed (i.e. by equity or by debt). In
addition, the Shareholder Loan is a separate contractual receivable owed by the Target
Company and will be separately assigned to the Purchaser on a dollar-for-dollar basis and
settled at par, without premium or discount. Following Closing, the Purchaser, being the
new sole shareholder of the Target Company, will step into the position of the Seller,
being the original lender, and assume the rights and obligations in respect of the
Shareholder Loan.
Accordingly, the total consideration of US$250,000,000 reflects the integrated
structure and commercial arrangement of the Acquisition, including both the standalone
value of the Target Company’s equity and the assignment of the Shareholder Loan,
ensuring the overall transaction economics are coherent with the Appraised Value and the
commercial negotiations between the parties. The Purchaser was able to secure a
consideration representing a discount of approximately 22% to the Appraised Value,
which it considers to be favourable for the Company and the Shareholders and would
enable the Group to maximize the return from the future business operations of the Target
Company and offer downside protection to the Purchaser for the potential integration risk.

Reasons for and Benefits of the Share Purchase Agreement
The Group is a biopharmaceutical company focused on the development,
manufacturing and commercialization of transformative pharmaceutical products
addressing critical unmet medical needs in Asian markets. As part of its long-term
strategy, the Group has been actively evaluating opportunities to acquire pharmaceutical
businesses in the Asia Pacific region with attractive market positions, clear growth
prospects and the potential to generate stable and sustainable returns that could generate
additional revenue synergies with its existing portfolio.
The Target Company mainly holds Marketing Authorization Holder (MAH) rights,
trademark and broad commercial rights to 14 branded chronic disease products across
multiple countries and regions in the Asia Pacific region, including South Korea,
Thailand, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Philippines, Malaysia and Australia and has established a
pan-Asia Pacific commercialization platform serving a large and growing chronic disease
patient population. There are over 2 billion people in the Group’s core Asia Pacific
market, with substantial unmet medical needs, particularly in chronic disease
management. The Group’s pipeline is also strategically focused on chronic disease
therapeutic areas, including cardiovascular, kidney and metabolic diseases, which creates
strong therapeutic, commercial and operational synergies with the Target Company’s
portfolio and platform.
Over the past three years, the Group has, through sustained investment and
execution, established a leading innovative-drug commercialization platform for chronic
diseases in China, as reflected in the strong sales performance of NEFECON®. The
Group’s strategic ambition is to build on this foundation and evolve into a leading
innovative-drug commercialization platform across Asia Pacific and, over time, a
prominent global biopharmaceutical company. Beyond Chinese Mainland, the Group’s
commercialized products, including NEFECON®, VELSIPITY® and XERAVA®, are
progressing through NDA approvals and reimbursement processes in authorized Asian
markets. The Acquisition would therefore accelerate the commercialization of the Group’s
existing products in Asian markets, support a faster ramp-up in overseas revenue
contribution, and represent an important step in the Group’s broader regional expansion
strategy.
The Acquisition of the Target Company can accelerate the Company’s
commercialization in Asia by transforming its emerging regional presence into a scaled,
revenue-generating platform. The Company already has a foundation across Hong Kong,
Macau, Taiwan, Singapore and Korea, with several innovative products entering a key

the Group’s Asia Pacific coverage to include Thailand, Malaysia, the Philippines,

and a mature cardiovascular/metabolic portfolio. This infrastructure can be leveraged to
accelerate launches of NEFECON®, XERAVA®, VELSIPITY® and future assets by
reducing country-by-country build-out time, improving local execution and strengthening
physician and payer access. Together, the combined platform can create a repeatable
‘‘China innovation to APAC’’ commercialization engine with greater control, scale and

The Group also believes that the coming years may represent an important window
of opportunity for the accelerated penetration of innovative medicines from Chinese
Mainland into the Asia Pacific region. Innovative medicines from Chinese Mainland are
increasingly competitive in clinical value, affordability and accessibility, which is
becoming more closely aligned with the needs of Asia Pacific healthcare systems and
patients. At the same time, regulatory pathways, market access frameworks and awareness
of innovative therapies across the region continue to improve. In such an environment,
long-term success is expected to depend not only on the quality of product assets, but also
on the ability to establish localized capabilities across registration, market access, medical
affairs and commercialization which would create a competitive advantage for the Group
in this growing region. The Acquisition will provide not only an established portfolio of
chronic disease products, but also a scalable commercial platform across key Asia Pacific
markets. The Target Company has accumulated local market knowledge, commercial
infrastructure, regulatory and access experience, distributor relationships and physician
networks in the region. These capabilities are expected to support the continued
commercialization of the Target Company’s existing products and may also provide a
foundation for the Group to accelerate the future launch and commercialization of its
existing and future innovative medicines in Asia Pacific.
Through the Acquisition, the Group would obtain the Target Company’s Asia Pacific
platform and its experienced local team of approximately 120 dedicated field forces,
enabling the Group to extend into the Asia Pacific region the commercialization
capabilities it has already built and validated in China. This would allow the Group to
strengthen its regional footprint, accelerate market entry and execution for both existing

The Acquisition is also expected to strengthen the Group’s business profile by adding

attractive commercial logic: it provides the Group with a ready-built regional platform,
deepens its presence in therapeutically aligned markets, and enhances its ability to
synergize future growth opportunities in Asia Pacific.

Valuation Methodology
The value analysis methods generally fall into three basic categories: the asset-based
approach, the market approach, and the income approach. The following provides a brief
introduction to these three value analysis methods:
(i) The asset-based approach refers to a general term for various valuation methods
that first calculate and analyze the replacement cost of assets, then assess and
quantify various depreciation factors already affecting those assets and finally
deduct these depreciation factors from the replacement cost to arrive at the
asset’s value. The fundamental premise of the asset-based approach is to
reconstruct or replace the asset itself. This analytical technique assumes that
any potential investor, when deciding whether to invest in an asset, will not be
willing to pay more than the current replacement cost of building that asset. If
the investment object is not brand new, the price the investor is willing to pay
will be the replacement cost of a brand-new asset minus various depreciation
factors. The asset-based approach is a widely used valuation methodology.
(ii) The market approach refers to a general term for various methods that use the
recent transaction prices of similar or comparable assets in the market and,
through direct comparison or analogous analysis, calculate the value of an asset.
The market approach is an appraisal technique that, based on the principle of
substitution, employs comparative and analogical reasoning and methodologies
to determine asset value. This analytical approach holds that any rational

[PDF PAGE 19]
investor, when acquiring an asset, would not be willing to pay more than the
current market price of a substitute asset with the same intended use. The
market approach is the most straightforward and persuasive valuation method.
(iii) The income approach refers to a general term for various analytical methods
that assess asset value by analyzing the present value of an asset’s expected
future earnings. The income approach employs capitalization and discounting
techniques and methodologies to evaluate and analyze asset value. This
valuation technique is based on the premise that any rational investor, when
acquiring or investing in an asset, will not be willing to pay or invest more than
the amount of money that the acquired or invested asset can generate in the
future, in other words, its expected returns. By utilizing technical tools such as
investment return analysis and discounted cash flow calculations, the income
approach takes the asset’s anticipated output capacity and profitability as the
key factors for analyzing and determining its value.
Given the characteristics of the Target Company, there are substantial limitations to
both the income approach and the cost approach in valuing the Target Company. In
particular:
(i) the income approach requires subjective assumptions to which the valuation is
highly sensitive, and even small changes in key inputs (such as discount rates,
growth assumptions, or project timing) may lead to significant fluctuations in
the valuation outcome;
(ii) the cost approach is based on the replacement or reproduction cost of the
underlying assets, which does not adequately capture the value of the Target
Company as going concern; and
(iii) the Target Company derives significant value from intangible factors such as
established operations as well as future earning potential, which are not fully
reflected under the cost approach.
In view of the above, the Valuer adopted the market approach for the valuation of
the Target Company. The market approach is applied to companies for which sufficient
and reliable comparable publicly listed companies can be identified, allowing market￾derived indicators to serve as appropriate basis for estimating value.
Given the characteristics of the Target Company, EV/EBITDA was adopted as the
primary valuation multiple. EV/EBITDA is widely used in valuing pharmaceutical
companies as it reflects the operating performance of the business before the impact of
capital structure, taxation and non-cash accounting items. In addition, EBITDA serves as
a proxy for the underlying cash generating ability of the Target Company. Compared with
net profit-based multiples, EV/EBITDA is less affected by differences in financing
arrangements, depreciation policies and tax positions across comparable companies,
thereby enhancing comparability.

The Valuer selected market comparables based on the following selection criteria:
(i) companies (a) in the pharmaceutical industry under industry category of S&P
Capital IQ Tree as extracted from Capital IQ database, and (b) whose products
are in relevant therapeutic areas. The screening process explicitly required: (i)
S&P Capital IQ classification as ‘‘Pharmaceuticals’’; (ii) core products covering
chronic disease areas such as cardiovascular and diabetes; and (iii) exclusion of
companies whose main products do not include hypertension or diabetes drugs;
(ii) companies with their core business based in greater China and Southeast Asia
territories;
(iii) companies listed in Hong Kong, Taiwan and other Southeast Asia territories.
The comparables cover three major stock exchanges, Hong Kong (4 companies),
Taiwan (2 companies) and Vietnam (2 companies), reflecting different market
pricing for similar pharmaceutical companies; and
(iv) companies with market capitalizations that are not significantly small in scale.
The comparable companies selected were China Medical System Holdings Limited,
Grand Pharmaceutical Group Limited, Luye Pharma Group Ltd., Simcere Pharmaceutical
Group Limited, Standard Chemical & Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., Lotus Pharmaceutical
Co., Ltd., DHG Pharmaceutical Joint Stock Company and Imexpharm Corporation. The
eight comparable companies comprise four Hong Kong-listed companies that are highly
comparable to the Target Company in terms of business model, therapeutic focus, and
commercial stage, as well as four Taiwan and Southeast Asian companies that serve as
supplementary comparables due to their regional relevance and similar product focus. The
eight companies are mature pharmaceutical enterprises with commercialized products,
stable operating cash flows and positive EBITDA, which is consistent with the Target
Company and represent a reasonable sample size in valuation practice, mitigating
idiosyncratic risks associated with any single company.
EV/EBITDA is used for all comparables, which eliminates the effects of capital
structure, depreciation policies and tax rates, directly reflecting operating cash flow
generation — directly comparable to the Target Company’s cash-generating ability. Key
financial indicators of the comparables are within a similar range to those of the Target
Company, further supporting comparability. The EV/EBITDA multiples of the comparable
companies as of the Valuation Date were approximately 12.8x, 11.5x, 6.4x, 15.6x, 7.3x,
12.2x, 10.0x and 14.6x, respectively. The adopted EV/EBITDA multiple was the median
of these multiples, being approximately 11.8x.
Computation of the Appraised Value
The Valuer applied the adopted EV/EBITDA multiple, being 11.8x, to the EBITDA
based on the management accounts of the Target Company for the year ended 31
December 2025, being US$27,546,000 (approximately RMB193,615,000). This resulted in
an indicative EV of approximately US$325,900,000 (approximately RMB2,290,686,000).

The Valuer then:
(i) added cash and cash equivalents based on the management accounts of
approximately US$400,000 (approximately RMB2,812,000) on the balance

(ii) applied a discount for lack of marketability (20.1%) and control premium
(23.9%) with reference to the Moore Control Premium & Discount for Lack of
Marketability Study. Discount for Lack of Marketability Study provides
industry-average discounts for lack of marketability based on empirical
transaction data, while Control Premium represents the average premium paid
for controlling interests in comparable arm’s-length transactions.
In calculating the equity value, debt and debt-like items are typically deducted.
However, taking into account that the Shareholder Loan will be assigned to the Purchaser

Value that reflects the full scope of what the Purchaser is acquiring (being both the Sale
Share and the assignment of the Shareholder Loan) and therefore better serves as a
reference for the determination of consideration.

Valuation Methodology
We have reviewed the Valuation Report and discussed with the Valuer
methodologies of, and bases and assumptions adopted for the Valuation, and
adjustments made to arrive at the Valuation. As advised by the Valuer, in arriving at
the fair value of 100% equity interest in the Target Company, the Valuer has
considered three generally accepted approaches, namely asset-based approach,
market approach and income approach.
(i) The asset-based approach refers to a general term for various valuation
methods that first calculate and analyze the replacement cost of assets,
then assess and quantify various depreciation factors already affecting
those assets and finally deduct these depreciation factors from the
replacement cost to arrive at the asset’s value. The fundamental premise of
the asset-based approach is to reconstruct or replace the asset itself. This
analytical technique assumes that any potential investor, when deciding
whether to invest in an asset, will not be willing to pay more than the
current replacement cost of building that asset. If the investment object is
not brand new, the price the investor is willing to pay will be the
replacement cost of a brand-new asset minus various depreciation factors.
The asset-based approach is a widely used valuation methodology.
(ii) The market approach refers to a general term for various methods that use
the recent transaction prices of similar or comparable assets in the market
and, through direct comparison or analogous analysis, calculate the value
of an asset. The market approach is an appraisal technique that, based on
the principle of substitution, employs comparative and analogical
reasoning and methodologies to determine asset value. This analytical
approach holds that any rational investor, when acquiring an asset, would
not be willing to pay more than the current market price of a substitute
asset with the same intended use. The market approach is the most
straightforward and persuasive valuation method.
(iii) The income approach refers to a general term for various analytical
methods that assess asset value by analyzing the present value of an asset’s
expected future earnings. The income approach employs capitalization and
discounting techniques and methodologies to evaluate and analyze asset
value. This valuation technique is based on the premise that any rational
investor, when acquiring or investing in an asset, will not be willing to pay
or invest more than the amount of money that the acquired or invested
asset can generate in the future, in other words, its expected returns. By
utilizing technical tools such as investment return analysis and discounted
cash flow calculations, the income approach takes the asset’s anticipated
output capacity and profitability as the key factors for analyzing and
determining its value.

The Valuer’s EBITDA calculation methodology follows the standard
calculation logic adopted by S&P Capital IQ, with underlying EBITDA figures
sourced from publicly disclosed annual reports, i.e. the Valuer defines EBITDA
as operating EBIT plus depreciation and amortization, and right-of-use asset
amortization. In comparison, our EBITDA is defined as net profit for the year
plus income tax expense, finance costs, depreciation and amortization, and
right-of-use asset amortization.
Having regard to the above differences in data sources and calculation
methodologies, all adopted data sources are reliable and both the Valuer and we
apply common market calculation practices on EV/EBITDA, we consider the
discrepancies in EV/EBITDA multiples to be reasonable and acceptable.
In addition, we have independently reviewed the publicly available information
of the remaining four Comparable Companies identified by the Valuer, and note that
(i) the remaining four Comparable Companies are companies listed in major stock
exchange, being Taiwan Stock Exchange and Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange; (ii) the
Comparable Companies share similarities with the Target Company in terms of
business and geographical focus; and (iii) the Valuer derived the EV/EBIDTA in the
same principle as described above. We note that two of the Comparable Companies
listed on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (HOSE) were selected pursuant to the
Selection Criteria within the Southeast Asia geographic scope. As discussed with the
Valuer, although companies across other major Southeast Asian markets (i.e.
Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia, and Vietnam) were also reviewed, only the Taiwan￾and Vietnam-listed companies were ultimately considered sufficiently comparable to
the Target Company based on their business activities, therapeutic focus, and
operational profile. Accordingly, notwithstanding that the Target Company does not
currently have any operations in Vietnam, Vietnam is an integral part of Southeast
Asia and the screening outcome is consistent with the Selection Criteria. We
therefore consider the selection of HOSE-listed Comparable Companies to be
reasonable and justified from a geographic perspective.
Having derived the EV/EBITDA multiple of each of the Comparable
Companies, the Valuer applied the median of the multiple to the Target Company’s
EBITDA for FY2025 to arrive at the enterprise value of the Target Company, which
was then converted to equity value by adding the Target Company’s cash and cash
equivalent and adjusted by discount on lack of marketability and control premium.
We understood that no adjustment was made for the Shareholder Loan in arriving at
the equity value of the Target Company. This is because the Shareholder Loan will
be assigned to the Purchaser on a dollar-to-dollar basis, and the Valuer considered

Discount for Lack of Marketability (‘‘DLOM’’)
As set out in the Valuation Report, liquidity refers to the marketability of equity
interests, that is, the speed and ease with which owners can convert their equity
interests into cash when they choose to sell them. The application of a discount for
lack of marketability reflects the fact that equity interests in private companies do
not have an established trading market. As a result, equity interests in private
companies are generally less readily marketable than those of publicly listed
companies. As the Target Company is not listed, the Valuer has applied a DLOM of
20.1%, with reference to the average DLOM figures from the Control Premium &
Discount for Lack of Marketability Study (February 2026) published by Moore Hong
Kong. Following our independent review, we note from the study that Moore Hong
Kong reviewed a total of 331 notifiable transaction circulars issued by listed
companies across various industries and published on the Stock Exchange website
for the trailing twelve months ended 31 December 2025. Of these 331 transactions,
only 33 included valuation reports with the adoption of DLOM adjustments. The
average DLOM of 20.1% was calculated by Moore Hong Kong based on this full set
of 33 relevant transactions, and we consider the sample size sufficient.
Control Premium
A controlling interest in a company provides significant advantages in decision￾making with respect to business operations and strategic development. In particular,
the holder of a controlling interest has the ability to influence the company’s cash
flow allocation and discretionary expenditures. As a result, a controlling interest
typically carries a higher value than a minority interest, which is subject to the
decisions, governance practices and management capabilities of the controlling
shareholders. The Valuer has adopted a control premium of 23.9%, with reference to
the average control premium figures from the Control Premium & Discount for Lack
of Marketability Study (February 2026) published by Moore Hong Kong. Following
our independent review, we note from the study that Moore Hong Kong reviewed a
total of 331 notifiable transaction circulars issued by listed companies across various
industries and published on the Stock Exchange website for the trailing twelve
months ended 31 December 2025. Of these 331 transactions, only 18 included
valuation reports with the adoption of control premium adjustments. The average
control premium of 23.9% was calculated by Moore Hong Kong based on this full
set of 18 relevant transactions, and we consider the sample size sufficient.
For our due diligence purpose, we independently searched the credential of
Moore Hong Kong and noted from its website that Moore Hong Kong, established in
1975, provides a full scope of services that include audit, assurance, accounting,
business outsourcing, tax and other advisory work. Meanwhile, Moore Hong Kong is

2.3 MATERIAL ACCOUNTING POLICY INFORMATION
Impairment of non-financial assets
Where an indication of impairment exists, or when annual impairment testing for an asset is required
(other than inventories and financial assets), the asset’s recoverable amount is estimated. An asset’s
recoverable amount is the higher of the asset’s or cash-generating unit’s value in use and its fair value less
costs of disposal, and is determined for an individual asset, unless the asset does not generate cash inflows
that are largely independent of those from other assets or groups of assets, in which case the recoverable
amount is determined for the cash-generating unit to which the asset belongs.
An impairment loss is recognised only if the carrying amount of an asset exceeds its recoverable
amount. In assessing value in use, the estimated future cash flows are discounted to their present value using
a pre-tax discount rate that reflects current market assessments of the time value of money and the risks
specific to the asset. An impairment loss is charged to profit or loss in the period in which it arises in those
expense categories consistent with the function of the impaired asset.
An assessment is made at the end of each reporting period as to whether there is an indication that
previously recognised impairment losses may no longer exist or may have decreased. If such an indication
exists, the recoverable amount is estimated. A previously recognised impairment loss of an asset other than
goodwill is reversed only if there has been a change in the estimates used to determine the recoverable
amount of that asset, but not to an amount higher than the carrying amount that would have been determined
(net of any depreciation/amortisation) had no impairment loss been recognised for the asset in prior years. A
reversal of such an impairment loss is credited to the profit or loss in the period in which it arises.
Related parties
A party is considered to be related to the Target Company if:
(a) the party is a person or a close member of that person’s family and that person
(i) has control or joint control over the Target Company;
(ii) has significant influence over the Target Company; or
(iii) is a member of the key management personnel of the Target Company or of a parent of the
Target Company;
or
(b) the party is an entity where any of the following conditions applies:
(i) the entity and the Target Company are members of the same group;
(ii) one entity is an associate or joint venture of the other entity (or of a parent, subsidiary or
fellow subsidiary of the other entity);
(iii) the entity and the Target Company are joint ventures of the same third party;
(iv) one entity is a joint venture of a third entity and the other entity is an associate of the third
entity;
(v) the entity is a post-employment benefit plan for the benefit of employees of either the
Target Company or an entity related to the Target Company;
(vi) the entity is controlled or jointly controlled by a person identified in (a);

Intangible assets
Intangible assets acquired separately are measured on initial recognition at cost. The useful lives of
intangible assets are assessed to be either finite or indefinite. Intangible assets with finite lives are
subsequently amortised over the useful economic life and assessed for impairment whenever there is an
indication that the intangible asset may be impaired. The amortisation period and the amortisation method for
an intangible asset with a finite useful life are reviewed at least at each financial year end.
Trademark and other rights
Trademark and other rights are stated at cost less any impairment losses and are amortised on the
straight-line basis over its estimated economic life of 20 years.
Investments and other financial assets
Initial recognition and measurement
Financial assets are classified, at initial recognition, as subsequently measured at amortised cost.
The classification of financial assets at initial recognition depends on the financial asset’s contractual
cash flow characteristics and the Target Company’s business model for managing them. With the exception of
trade receivables that do not contain a significant financing component or for which the Target Company has
applied the practical expedient of not adjusting the effect of a significant financing component, the Target
Company initially measures a financial asset at its fair value plus transaction costs. Trade receivables that do
not contain a significant financing component or for which the Target Company has applied the practical
expedient are measured at the transaction price determined under IFRS 15 in accordance with the policies set
out for ‘‘Revenue recognition’’ below.
In order for a financial asset to be classified and measured at amortised cost, it needs to give rise to
cash flows that are solely payments of principal and interest (‘‘SPPI’’) on the principal amount outstanding.
The Target Company’s business model for managing financial assets refers to how it manages its
financial assets in order to generate cash flows. The business model determines whether cash flows will result
from collecting contractual cash flows, selling the financial assets, or both. Financial assets classified and
measured at amortised cost are held within a business model with the objective to hold financial assets in
order to collect contractual cash flows.
Purchases or sales of financial assets that require delivery of assets within the period generally
established by regulation or convention in the marketplace are recognised on the trade date, that is, the date
that the Target Company commits to purchase or sell the asset.
Subsequent measurement
The subsequent measurement of financial assets depends on their classification as follows:
Financial assets at amortised cost (debt instruments)
Financial assets at amortised cost are subsequently measured using the effective interest method and are
subject to impairment. Gains and losses are recognised in profit or loss when the asset is derecognised,
modified or impaired.

Derecognition of financial assets
A financial asset (or, where applicable, a part of a financial asset or part of a group of similar financial
assets) is primarily derecognised (i.e., removed from the Target Company’s statement of financial position)
when:
. the rights to receive cash flows from the asset have expired; or
. the Target Company has transferred its rights to receive cash flows from the asset or has assumed
an obligation to pay the received cash flows in full without material delay to a third party under a
‘‘pass-through’’ arrangement; and either (a) the Target Company has transferred substantially all
the risks and rewards of the asset, or (b) the Target Company has neither transferred nor retained
substantially all the risks and rewards of the asset, but has transferred control of the asset.
Impairment of financial assets
The Target Company recognises an allowance for expected credit losses (‘‘ECLs’’) for all debt
instruments. ECLs are based on the difference between the contractual cash flows due in accordance with the
contract and all the cash flows that the Target Company expects to receive, discounted at an approximation of
the original effective interest rate. The expected cash flows will include cash flows from the sale of collateral
held or other credit enhancements that are integral to the contractual terms.
General approach
ECLs are recognised in two stages. For credit exposures for which there has not been a significant
increase in credit risk since initial recognition, ECLs are provided for credit losses that result from default
events that are possible within the next 12 months (a 12-month ECL). For those credit exposures for which
there has been a significant increase in credit risk since initial recognition, a loss allowance is required for
credit losses expected over the remaining life of the exposure, irrespective of the timing of the default (a
lifetime ECL).
At each reporting date, the Target Company assesses whether the credit risk on a financial instrument
has increased significantly since initial recognition. When making the assessment, the Target Company
compares the risk of a default occurring on the financial instrument as at the reporting date with the risk of a
default occurring on the financial instrument as at the date of initial recognition and considers reasonable and
supportable information that is available without undue cost or effort, including historical and forward￾looking information. The Target Company considers that there has been a significant increase in credit risk
when contractual payments are more than 30 days past due.
The Target Company considers a financial asset in default when contractual payments are 90 days past
due. However, in certain cases, the Target Company may also consider a financial asset to be in default when
internal or external information indicates that the Target Company is unlikely to receive the outstanding
contractual amounts in full before taking into account any credit enhancements held by the Target Company.
A financial asset is written off when there is no reasonable expectation of recovering the contractual
cash flows.
Financial assets at amortised cost are subject to impairment under the general approach and they are
classified within the following stages for measurement of ECLs except for trade receivables which apply the
simplified approach as detailed below.
Stage 1 — Financial instruments for which credit risk has not increased significantly since initial
recognition and for which the loss allowance is measured at an amount equal to 12-
month ECLs

Simplified approach
For trade receivables that do not contain a significant financing component or when the Target
Company applies the practical expedient of not adjusting the effect of a significant financing component, the
Target Company applies the simplified approach in calculating ECLs. Under the simplified approach, the
Target Company does not track changes in credit risk, but instead recognises a loss allowance based on
lifetime ECLs at each reporting date. The Target Company makes reference to the credit loss experience of
similar companies in the market for estimation of ECLs, adjusted for forward-looking factors specific to the
debtors and the economic environment.
Financial liabilities
Initial recognition and measurement
Financial liabilities are classified, at initial recognition, as loans and borrowings or payables, as
appropriate.
All financial liabilities are recognised initially at fair value and, in the case of loans and borrowings and
payables, net of directly attributable transaction costs.
The Target Company’s financial liabilities include trade and other payables and amounts due to a
related party.
Subsequent measurement
The subsequent measurement of financial liabilities depends on their classification as follows:
Financial liabilities at amortised cost (trade and other payable and amounts due to a related party)
After initial recognition, trade and other payables and amounts due to a related party are subsequently
measured at amortised cost, using the effective interest rate method unless the effect of discounting would be
immaterial, in which case they are stated at cost. Gains and losses are recognised in profit or loss when the
liabilities are derecognised as well as through the effective interest rate amortisation process.
Amortised cost is calculated by taking into account any discount or premium on acquisition and fees or
costs that are an integral part of the effective interest rate. The effective interest rate amortisation is included
in finance costs in profit or loss.
Derecognition of financial liabilities
A financial liability is derecognised when the obligation under the liability is discharged or cancelled,
or expires.
When an existing financial liability is replaced by another from the same lender on substantially
different terms, or the terms of an existing liability are substantially modified, such an exchange or
modification is treated as a derecognition of the original liability and a recognition of a new liability, and the
difference between the respective carrying amounts is recognised in profit or loss.

Inventories
Inventories are stated at the lower of cost and net realisable value. Cost is determined on the specific
identification method and, in the case of finished goods, comprises direct materials and an appropriate
proportion of overheads. Net realisable value is based on estimated selling prices less any estimated costs to
be incurred to completion and disposal.
Cash and cash equivalents
For the purpose of the statement of cash flows, cash and cash equivalents comprise cash at banks.
Income tax
Income tax comprises current and deferred tax. Income tax relating to items recognised outside profit or
loss is recognised outside profit or loss, either in other comprehensive income or directly in equity.
Current tax assets and liabilities are measured at the amount expected to be recovered from or paid to
the taxation authorities, based on tax rates (and tax laws) that have been enacted or substantively enacted by
the end of the reporting period, taking into consideration interpretations and practices prevailing in the
country in which the Target Company operates.
Deferred tax is provided, using the liability method, on all temporary differences at the end of the
reporting period between the tax bases of assets and liabilities and their carrying amounts for financial
reporting purposes.
Deferred tax liabilities are recognised for all taxable temporary differences, except when the deferred
tax liability arises from the initial recognition of an asset or liability in a transaction that is not a business
combination and, at the time of the transaction, affects neither the accounting profit nor taxable profit or loss
and does not give rise to equal taxable and deductible temporary differences.
Deferred tax assets are recognised for all deductible temporary differences, and the carryforward of
unused tax credits and any unused tax losses. Deferred tax assets are recognised to the extent that it is
probable that taxable profit will be available against which the deductible temporary differences, and the
carryforward of unused tax credits and unused tax losses can be utilised, except when the deferred tax asset
relating to the deductible temporary differences arises from the initial recognition of an asset or liability in a
transaction that is not a business combination and, at the time of the transaction, affects neither the accounting
profit nor taxable profit or loss and does not give rise to equal taxable and deductible temporary differences;
and
The carrying amount of deferred tax assets is reviewed at the end of each reporting period and reduced
to the extent that it is no longer probable that sufficient taxable profit will be available to allow all or part of
the deferred tax asset to be utilised. Unrecognised deferred tax assets are reassessed at the end of each
reporting period and are recognised to the extent that it has become probable that sufficient taxable profit will
be available to allow all or part of the deferred tax asset to be recovered.
Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured at the tax rates that are expected to apply to the period
when the asset is realised or the liability is settled, based on tax rates (and tax laws) that have been enacted or
substantively enacted by the end of the reporting period.
Revenue recognition
Revenue from contracts with customers
Revenue from contracts with customers is recognised when control of goods or services is transferred to
the customers at an amount that reflects the consideration to which the Target Company expects to be entitled
in exchange for those goods or services.

Sale of pharmaceutical products
Revenue from the sale of pharmaceutical products is recognised at the point in time when control of the
asset is transferred to the customer, generally on acceptance of the pharmaceutical products by customers.
Royalty income
For the arrangement that includes sales-based royalties, the Target Company recognises revenue when
the related sales occur.
Borrowing costs
All borrowing costs are expensed in the period in which they are incurred.
Foreign currencies
The Historical Financial Information is presented in USD, which is the functional currency of the
Target Company. Foreign currency transactions recorded by the Target Company are initially recorded using
its functional currency rates prevailing at the dates of the transactions. Monetary assets and liabilities
denominated in foreign currencies are translated at the functional currency rates of exchange ruling at the end
of the reporting period. Differences arising on settlement or translation of monetary items are recognised in
profit or loss.
Non-monetary items that are measured in terms of historical cost in a foreign currency are translated
using the exchange rates at the dates of the initial transactions. Non-monetary items measured at fair value in
a foreign currency are translated using the exchange rates at the date when the fair value was measured. The
gain or loss arising on translation of a non-monetary item measured at fair value is treated in line with the
recognition of the gain or loss on change in fair value of the item (i.e., translation difference on the item
whose fair value gain or loss is recognised in other comprehensive income or profit or loss is also recognised
in other comprehensive income or profit or loss, respectively).

4. VALUE ANALYSIS METHODS
4.1 General Value Analysis Method
The value analysis methods generally fall into three basic categories: the asset-based
approach, the market approach, and the income approach. The following provides a brief
introduction to these three value analysis methods:
The asset-based approach refers to a general term for various valuation methods that
first calculate and analyze the replacement cost of assets, then assess and quantify various
depreciation factors already affecting those assets and finally deduct these depreciation
factors from the replacement cost to arrive at the asset’s value. The fundamental premise
of the asset-based approach is to reconstruct or replace the asset itself. This analytical
technique assumes that any potential investor, when deciding whether to invest in an
asset, will not be willing to pay more than the current replacement cost of building that
asset. If the investment object is not brand new, the price the investor is willing to pay
will be the replacement cost of a brand-new asset minus various depreciation factors. The
asset-based approach is a widely used valuation methodology. The asset-based approach
refers to a general term for various valuation methods that first calculate and analyze the
replacement cost of assets, then assess and quantify various depreciation factors already
affecting those assets and finally deduct these depreciation factors from the replacement
cost to arrive at the asset’s value. The fundamental premise of the asset-based approach is
to reconstruct or replace the asset itself. This analytical technique assumes that any
potential investor, when deciding whether to invest in an asset, will not be willing to pay
more than the current replacement cost of building that asset. If the investment object is
not brand-new, the price the investor is willing to pay will be the replacement cost of a
brand-new asset minus various depreciation factors. The asset-based approach is a widely
used valuation methodology.
APPENDIX V VALUATION REPORT
– V-5 –

[PDF PAGE 108]
The market approach refers to a general term for various methods that use the recent
transaction prices of similar or comparable assets in the market and, through direct
comparison or analogous analysis, calculate the value of an asset. The market approach is
an appraisal technique that, based on the principle of substitution, employs comparative
and analogical reasoning and methodologies to determine asset value. This analytical
approach holds that any rational investor, when acquiring an asset, would not be willing
to pay more than the current market price of a substitute asset with the same intended use.
The market approach is the most straightforward and persuasive valuation method.
The income approach refers to a general term for various analytical methods that
assess asset value by analyzing the present value of an asset’s expected future earnings.
The income approach employs capitalization and discounting techniques and
methodologies to evaluate and analyze asset value. This valuation technique is based on
the premise that any rational investor, when acquiring or investing in an asset, will not be
willing to pay or invest more than the amount of money that the acquired or invested
asset can generate in the future, in other words, its expected returns. By utilizing technical
tools such as investment return analysis and discounted cash flow calculations, the income
approach takes the asset’s anticipated output capacity and profitability as the key factors
for analyzing and determining its value.
Given the characteristics of the Target Company, there are substantial limitations to
both the income approach and the cost approach in valuing the Target Company. In
particular:
(i) the income approach requires subjective assumptions to which the valuation is
highly sensitive, and even small changes in key inputs (such as discount rates,
growth assumptions, or project timing) may lead to significant fluctuations in
the valuation outcome;
(ii) the cost approach is based on the replacement or reproduction cost of the
underlying assets, which does not adequately capture the value of the Target
Company as going concerns; and
(iii) the Target Company derive significant value from intangible factors such as
established operations, market position and company relationships, as well as
their future earning potential, which are not fully reflected under the cost
approach.
In view of the above, we have adopted the market approach for the valuation of the
Target Company. The market approach is applied to company for which sufficient and
reliable comparable publicly listed company can be identified, allowing market-derived
indicators to serve as appropriate basis for estimating value.

4.2 Market Approach — Market Multiple Method
4.2.1 Selection of the Value Multiple
The value multiple typically includes profitability ratios, asset ratios, revenue
ratios, and other specific ratios. When selecting, calculating, and applying value
ratios, we generally take into account:
. The value multiple for selection helps to reasonably determine the value of
the valuation analysis subject.
. The data scope and the calculation method for the value multiple are
consistent.
Based on a comprehensive comparative analysis and assessment of the Target
Company’s industry and its own financial condition, we have selected the most
appropriate valuation multiple for this valuation analysis. The specific reasons for
our selection are as follows:
Given the characteristics of the Target Company, EV/EBITDA is adopted as the
primary valuation multiple. EV/EBITDA is widely used in the valuation of
pharmaceutical companies because it reflects the operating performance of a
business before the effects of capital structure, taxes, and non-cash accounting
items. Furthermore, EBITDA serves as a proxy for the underlying cash-generating
ability of the target company. Compared with multiples based on net profit, EV/
EBITDA is less affected by differences in financing arrangements, depreciation
policies, and tax positions among comparable companies, thereby enhancing
comparability.

4.3 Other Valuation Considerations
4.3.1 Discount for Lack of Marketability (‘‘DLOM’’)
Liquidity refers to the marketability of equity interests, that is, the speed and
ease with which owners can convert their equity interests into cash when they choose
to sell them. The application of a discount for lack of marketability reflects the fact
APPENDIX V VALUATION REPORT
– V-11 –

[PDF PAGE 114]
that equity interests in private companies do not have an established trading market.
As a result, equity interests in private companies are generally less readily
marketable than those of publicly listed companies. Accordingly, the value of equity
interests in a private company is typically lower than that of comparable equity
interests in publicly listed companies.
In this valuation analysis, where the market approach using the market multiple
method is applied, the discount for lack of marketability of 20.1% is adopted, with
reference to the average DLOM figures from the Moore Control Premium &
Discount for Lack of Marketability Study issued in February 2026 representing the
average statistics reported in the study for the trailing 12-month period ended 31
December 2025.
4.3.2 Control Premium (‘‘CP’’)
A controlling interest in a company provides significant advantages in decision￾making with respect to business operations and strategic development. In particular,
the holder of a controlling interest has the ability to influence the company’s cash
flow allocation and discretionary expenditures. As a result, a controlling interest
typically carries a higher value than a minority interest, which is subject to the
decisions, governance practices and management capabilities of the controlling
shareholders.
In this valuation analysis, where the market approach using the market multiple
method is applied, the control premium of 23.9% is adopted, with reference to the
average CP figures from the Moore Control Premium & Discount for Lack of
Marketability Study issued in February 2026 representing the average statistics
reported in the study for the trailing 12-month period ended 31 December 2025.
100% Equity Value (before shareholder loan) on non-marketable and controlling
basis = Equity Value (pre adjustment)*(1–DLOM)*(1+CP).
